title: Drawback Chess, But I KNOW My Drawbacks
summary: Online Drawback Chess (drawback chess site) vs anonymous humans, but this time the narrator can SEE his own drawback. Goal: win three games. Game 1 (Black, opponent 'Don't Be a Fool, Don't Reveal'): his drawback 'Triple Play' - he can only capture the enemy king if he has three knights; opponent's was 'Absolution' (after a non-bishop piece captures, it must end its next turn adjacent to one of your bishops). Game 2: his drawback 'Ivory Tower' (you lose if an opposing piece is adjacent to your king); opponent's 'Wind-up toys' (after the first 12 moves you can't move knights and bishops). Intro examples: 'Boxing with shadows' (must move to the square your opponent just moved from), 'Checkers' (if you can capture, you must).
rules: Standard start; Drawback Chess king-capture rules (no check; capture the king to win; resignations count).
Each side gets one random drawback; the player's own drawback is visible to him in this episode, the opponent's hidden until the end.

Drawbacks seen: Triple Play (can only capture the enemy king if you own three knights); Absolution (when a non-bishop piece captures it must next move to a square adjacent to one of your bishops); Ivory Tower (you lose if an opposing piece is adjacent to your king); Wind-up toys (after the first 12 moves you can't move your knights and bishops); Boxing with shadows; Checkers.
Some drawbacks can be 'evaporated' (e.g. get rid of your queen by move 11).
win_condition: Capture the opponent's king (subject to own drawback), or opponent loses via their drawback/resigns; goal win three games.
